Subject: NorthStar - deployment/residency follow-up and next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of items we need clarified to recommend the right serving mode: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem.

Recap from our side:
- Use case: customer-facing fraud-alert enrichment and internal KYC assistant (low-volume bursts, PII in prompts).
- Primary region: EU (data residency requirement under internal policy).
- Secondary region: occasional APAC users via partner flows — must confirm if cross-border requests are allowed.

Questions we need answers to before we scope a PoC / cost estimate:
1) Does NorthStar require that raw request/response data (and logs) never leave EU territories? Or is processing in EU with encrypted telemetry to US control plane allowed?
2) Do you need dedicated GPU capacity for consistent throughput (predictable SLAs), or would you consider a Private VPC with customer-managed network and HSM for keys?
3) For APAC traffic: do you need local processing in APAC region, or is low-latency fall back to EU acceptable?

Proposed next steps:
- If residency must be strict EU-only for all processing and logs, recommend Private VPC / on-prem install.
- If control-plane residency is negotiable (control plane in US, data plane in EU), we can offer Hosted EU region + VPC peering for audit logs.
- I'll loop Ben for procurement/discount conversations and Karthik for technical feasibility and timeline for a Private VPC pilot.

Attachments: NSB_RFP_AppendixA.pdf (attachment stub) — I put the RFP you mentioned into our drive.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call with your compliance folks if helpful.

Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Sofia — thanks for the summary and clear questions. A few clarifications from Compliance/Procurement side: 

1) Residency: NorthStar policy requires that customer data and any unredacted logs remain within the EU. Metadata can be replicated outside EU only if encrypted with customer keys and permitted by our legal team.

2) We are open to either Dedicated capacity or Private VPC. Key requirements: full audit trail, HSM integration for key control (we manage keys), and the ability to run annual third-party penetration tests.

3) APAC: inbound partner flows are low volume and can be routed to EU if latency is acceptable. If we run a pilot and latency proves an issue, we will evaluate a small Dedicated presence in APAC later.

Procurement asks: can you provide a short document listing differences in admin controls and compliance guarantees between Dedicated vs Private VPC (especially around key ownership, log residency, and support for third-party audits)? Also need lead time estimates for a Private VPC pilot and ballpark cost ranges for a 6-month PoC.

Elena / Sofia / Ben — quick feasibility note from engineering/solutions perspective.

Summary of options (technical):
- Hosted EU (Redwood-managed hosted inference in EU regions): easiest to onboard, short lead time (days). We can guarantee data plane processing in EU. However, control-plane and aggregated telemetry typically run in our central control plane; we can offer log redaction and customer-side encryption for telemetry. Not ideal for strict EU-only log residency.

- Dedicated Capacity (reserved GPU pools in an EU region): Redwood-managed infra, stronger contractual guarantees for locality and SLAs. We support customer KMS via HSM integration (bring-your-own-key) with per-request envelope encryption. Lead time: 2-4 weeks to provision a small reserved pool and validate network peering.

- Private VPC / On-prem (customer-managed network or on-prem package): full data and log residency in-customer network. We support a Private control plane option where control signals can be routed through a customer-hosted control endpoint. This meets the strictest compliance needs but requires 4-8 weeks for environment setup, HSM integration, and pen test scheduling.

Cross-region routing / APAC flows:
- We can route partner requests to EU processing via routing policy. If latency to APAC is unacceptable, we can provision a small Dedicated pool in APAC later and replicate models/artifacts; replication maintains model version parity but not logs.

Pilot suggestions:
- Phase 0: Compliance checklist & SOW + timeline (1 week).
- Phase 1: Private VPC pilot in EU with HSM keywrap, sample dataset, and smoke tests (4-6 weeks).
- Phase 2: Measure latency for partner flows and decide on APAC Dedicated pilot (follow-on).

I can draft the technical appendix for the comparison doc (include network diagrams, KMS/HSM flow, and log-handling patterns). Attaching an internal summary spreadsheet: redwood-hosting-options-summary.xlsx (attachment stub).

- Karthik
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
